To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a simple and safer solution deposition process for CIGS is presented that uses a diamine/ditiothiol mixture to deposit the metal sulfides, and that the resulting films are selenized in a two-stage process, resulting in power conversion effi ciencies of up to 10.1%.
we have developed a safer and simpler solution deposition process for the preparation of CIGS solar cells, based on the use of metal sulfide precursor solutions.
a simple and safer solution deposition approach for CuIn(S, S2e)2 thin film solar cells has been developed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a simple, safe, and scalable method for the solution processing of CIGS absorbers.
the development of a safer and more environmentally friendly approach to the solution processing of CuIn(S,se)2 absorbers for photovoltaics.
a simple and hydrazine-free solution-based deposition of CuIn(S,se)2 solar cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of a metal chalcogenide spray solution in combination with a simple selenization process is an effective and safer alternative to the hydrazine-based approach for the fabrication of high quality CuIn(S,se)2 absorbers for thin film solar cells.
we have developed a safer and more environmentally friendly method for solution deposition of CIGS solar cells.
the use of metal chalcogenide solutions for the solution deposition of CuIn(S,se)2 absorbers in a hydrazine-free process has been demonstrated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a simple method to deposit high-quality CuInSe2 thin films by solution processing in a diamine-dithiol mixture.

we have shown that CuIn(S,se)2 solar cells can be deposited from metal sulfide precursors without hydrazine and that the resulting solar cells can reach efficiencies of 8% without any postdeposition anneal.
a hydrazine-free, low-cost solution process has been developed for the fabrication of CuIn(S,se)2 solar cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple, low-cost, hydrazine-free approach to deposit CuIn(S, Sc)2 can be used for the fabrication of high-quality solar cells.
a simple and safer approach to deposit CIGS absorbers is now possible, which could be further improved with additional optimization.

the use of metal sulfide precursors in a diamine/ dithiol solvent system is a promising approach for the solution processing of CIGS, which is compatible with the use of a chromatography atomization system.
